title: Rinnegackonck
summary: Rinnegackonck is a Brooklyn placename associated with the plantation of George Rapaljee and early Dutch records near western Long Island.
introduction_content: Rinnegackonck, also written Rinnegakonck and Rinnegaconk, is recorded as a tract of land associated with the plantation of George Rapaljee in Brooklyn.
history_content: The name appears in Dutch colonial records describing land near Rapaljee's plantation and toward Mespaechtes. Dated records appear in the Historic Timeline with citation notes.
translation_content:
Rinnegackonck is interpreted as on the pleasant land or a delightful place, from elements connected with pleasant, land, and a locative ending.

Why Place Names Matter

“Whether a name’s born of whimsy or faith, whether it was first written down by a cavalier in his log or a bureaucrat in a city hall, its “impression and enchantment” derives, too, from the truth that its meaning can’t be fully divorced from its roots.”

— Joshua Jelly-Schapiro, Why Place-Names Matter (2025), Opening essay
preservation_content: Rinnegackonck preserves an early Brooklyn placename from the Dutch colonial record, linking Native place geography with land transactions around the western Long Island frontier.
